habitat: Flocks on floodplains, estuaries, lakesides and farmlands.
summary: A locally common summer resident. Dark brown above, with a buff throat edged black, a buff breast, and a white belly and rump. The underwing coverts are rufous and the secondaries are white-tipped. At rest the tail projects beyond the wingtips, and the base of the bill is redder, and less black, than Black-winged Pratincole. Newman does not describe the voice. Months were left unset. The Kemp name is Redwinged Pratincole and the code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Black-winged Pratincole has entirely blackish underwings and less red on the gape. Collared Pratincole has rufous underwing coverts and white-tipped secondaries.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^4=16 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 8–32.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

bill.shape: Base redder, and less black, than Black-winged Pratincole.

wings.pattern: Rufous underwing coverts and white-tipped secondaries.

tail.shape: Projects beyond the wingtips at rest.

viewNotes.note: Dark brown above, buff throat edged black, and a redder bill base.
Buff throat with a black edge, and a buff breast.
Dark brown upper parts and a white rump. The tail projects beyond the wingtips.
Rufous underwing coverts and white-tipped secondaries. Flocks wheel in columns.
Rufous underwings, a buff breast and a white belly.

calls.description: Newman’s species page does not describe the voice. Grade A call and flight call from Arles, France. The filename is French, glareole a collier.
